note: Wealth and income distribution. CRITICAL MEASUREMENT NOTE: top-1% wealth-share levels differ across measures. Fed DFA (quarterly, includes all assets net of pensions differently) shows top 1% ~30% (1989) → ~30.5% (Q1 2024), with a mid-30s peak ~2015-16. Saez-Zucman (capitalized income/estate method, includes offshore) shows ~25-26% (1980) → ~40-42% (2020s). SCF (survey) ~30% (1989) → ~34-35% (2022). The DIRECTION of change since ~1980 is unanimous across all measures; the level and the timing differ. Report ranges, never a single false-precise number.

top1_wealth_share_pct.note: Ranges across measures; see header note. 1989/2024 DFA values verified.

fed_dfa.note: Quarterly; values at year-end approx; Q1 2024 = 30.5% verified. Top 0.1% ~14.5% (2025).

saez_zucman.note: Capitalized-income method; approximate benchmark values from published series.

scf.note: Survey of Consumer Finances triennial; approximate.

top1_income_share_pct.note: Piketty-Saez-Zucman series, approximate benchmarks; excl. transfers. 1980 trough ~10-11% → ~19-21% recent.

gini_household_income.note: Census CPS ASEC money income; approx values; 2021 near record (0.494).

middle_class_share.note: Pew definition: 2/3 to 2x median household income. 1971 and 2023 verified; 2021 value from Pew 2022 report.

middle_class_income_share.unit: % of aggregate household income going to middle-income households

union_density_pct.note: BLS; 1983 first year of current series; ~10% recent. Private-sector density ~6%.

stock_ownership_concentration.unit: % of corporate equities & mutual funds held
stock_ownership_concentration.note: Fed SCF/DFA: top 10% hold ~89-92% of directly+indirectly held equities; top 1% ~50%. Widely cited (inequality.org).

median_wealth_usd.note: Approximate (SCF/DFA). Median wealth rose sharply 2019-2021 (home equity + asset appreciation + savings) then roughly flat.

homeownership_pct.note: Census HVS; 2004-2006 bubble peak; post-2008 trough; recent ~65-66%.
